ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The image shows a transition-state structure with a left EtO fragment, a fused bicyclic carbon framework in the center, a CN substituent attached near the upper transition-state carbon, an exocyclic imine-like C=N/NH group extending to the right, and a right OEt fragment. Curved arrows and explicitly shown hydrogens/proton-transfer features are present, but the question says to disregard arrows and exclude bonds involving hydrogen. Reasoning: Partitioning the drawing as specified: the left EtO fragment contributes 2 heavy-atom bonds; the fused bicyclic carbon framework contributes 10 heavy-atom ring bonds; the CN substituent contributes 2 heavy-atom bonds, namely the C-C attachment plus the C≡N connection; the exocyclic imine C=N contributes 1 heavy-atom bond; and the right OEt fragment contributes 2 heavy-atom bonds. Excluding N-H, O-H, C-H or H-transfer bonds, the total is 2 + 10 + 2 + 1 + 2 = 17.

method.method_draft: Start with the fused-ring topology visible in the image: a cyclohexene ring fused to a cyclopentane ring shares one C-C edge, so the heavy-atom ring framework has 6 + 5 - 1 = 10 bonds, regardless of the alkene being double. Then add all heavy-atom bonds outside the rings: 2 for the left EtO group, 2 for the right OEt group, 2 for the nitrile substituent, and 1 for the exocyclic C=N bond to NH. Do not add the N-H or O-H connections and ignore arrows. Total = 10 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 1 = 17.
